items.title: Jack White Covers “Jolene” Live in Tribute to Dolly Parton: Watch
items.summary:
Jack White covered "Jolene" during a concert in London on Tuesday night, hours after news broke that Dolly Parton had died at 80. White led his band through the song and, as the performance ended, pointed to the sky and made the sign of the cross. He posted video of the moment to Instagram.

According to Consequence, which cited Setlist.fm, it was the first time White had performed "Jolene" since 2007. The song was a fixture of White Stripes shows in the band's earlier years, and their version was released as the B-side to the single "Hello Operator." Parton herself called the White Stripes rendition one of the greatest versions ever recorded.

White's written tribute was brief. "Instant Sainthood," he wrote of Parton in an Instagram post after her death.

His label, Third Man Records, issued a longer statement focused on Parton's work away from music. "Dolly's legacy goes far beyond the music," it read, citing her Imagination Library, which put millions of books into children's hands, along with her support for education, literacy, disaster relief and communities in need. The statement called her "an incredible artist, philanthropist, advocate, and human being."

Parton died Tuesday at 80. Tributes have come in steadily since from across the music and film industries, with White's performance among the first to arrive from the stage rather than a social media post.

items.title: Dolly Parton Honored by Kacey Musgraves, Keith Urban, Reba McEntire: ‘We Will Always Love Her’
items.summary:
Musicians, actors and country music institutions spent the day after Dolly Parton's death publishing tributes to the singer, who died Aug. 25. Variety collected statements from Kacey Musgraves, Keith Urban, Reba McEntire, Jane Fonda, Julia Roberts, Sally Field, Colman Domingo and others, along with a formal statement from the Academy of Country Music.

Musgraves, who performed with Parton at an all-star tribute during the 2019 Grammy Awards, wrote on X: "Dolly. This really really hurts. The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden. So glad she's with her Carl Dean. No one talk to me today." Urban posted to his Instagram Stories that he was "heartbroken today" and had "no words right now."

McEntire shared a photo of the two of them and wrote a longer note. "Dolly, thank you for all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth," she wrote, adding that she would never forget the first time she met Parton or their last conversation. She closed, "I will always love you, Reba."

Parton's film collaborators also spoke. Roberts, her "Steel Magnolias" co-star, said in a statement that "Dolly was a magical and joyous human" and that "the sun has dimmed today." Field, also from that film, called her one of the "angels on earth." Fonda, who worked with Parton on "9 to 5" and later on "Grace and Frankie," wrote a lengthy remembrance describing her as "simultaneously a naughty, playful southern gal from the hollows of Tennessee and a deep, soulful thinker," and addressed Parton's LGBTQ+ fans directly: "I want you to know that she loved you."

The Academy of Country Music noted that Parton, a member of the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Grand Ole Opry, won 14 ACM Awards and hosted the ceremony three times. The organization gave her its Poet's Award at this year's ACM Honors. CEO emeritus Damon Whiteside said working with Parton on the 2022 and 2023 broadcasts and presenting that award to her last week were career highlights.

items.title: Rupert Grint to Join Broadway Cast of ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’
items.summary:
Rupert Grint will join the Broadway cast of "Harry Potter and the Cursed Child," playing the adult Ron Weasley — the same character he originated across the eight "Harry Potter" films. He begins Feb. 2, 2027, for a 17-week run at the Lyric Theatre that ends May 30.

Grint framed the return around where he is in his own life. "Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old and I can't wait to meet him again in this stage of life," he said. "There is something so full-circle and so special about stepping back into Ron's shoes now when we are both fathers; it is somehow both very familiar and completely new."

He is the second film cast member to move into the stage production. Tom Felton, who played Draco Malfoy on screen, is currently in the play and set to continue through Jan. 3, 2027. The Hollywood Reporter noted that Felton's casting sent the show's box office climbing sharply.

Grint has worked on stage before, appearing on Broadway in the 2014 production of "It's Only a Play" alongside Matthew Broderick and Nathan Lane, and in the West End in Jez Butterworth's "Mojo" with Ben Whishaw. His screen credits include M. Night Shyamalan's "Servant" for Apple TV, Hanna Bergholm's "Nightborn," which premiered at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival, and Paramount's "Ebenezer," opening this fall.

Producers Sonia Friedman and Colin Callender said Grint is "not simply revisiting a role from his past" but "continuing a journey he began as a child," and described his casting as a bridge between the original story and the play's themes of family, legacy and the passage of time.

items.title: Eminem Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton: “A Superstar in Every Sense”
items.summary:
Eminem marked Dolly Parton's death at 80 by posting a letter she wrote to him after the two were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in the same class in 2022. The rapper shared the note on social media, noting that despite sharing the honor, they never met.

"I'm sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had an impact on me," he wrote. "She definitely didn't have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense. Rest easy Dolly. And thank you for the kind words."

In the letter, which Consequence reported on, Parton addressed him as Marshall and congratulated him on the induction and on his performance at the ceremony — a medley of "My Name Is," "Rap God," "Forever" and "Not Afraid," plus "Sing for the Moment" with Steven Tyler and "Stan" with Ed Sheeran. "Even though I don't know a lot about rap music, I've come to know that you are the very best at it," she wrote. "I have always felt some unexplained connection to you like I know you somehow."

Parton wrote that she had hoped to find him at the ceremony but lost the chance in the commotion. "Maybe someday we'll meet," she said, adding that he should keep going because "no matter how complex your world may be just know you are very special and touch people in ways you don't even know."

The 2022 class also included Lionel Richie, Carly Simon, Eurythmics, Duran Duran and Pat Benatar with Neil Giraldo. Dr. Dre inducted Eminem, who was eligible for the first time, and P!NK inducted Parton, who had initially tried to withdraw from consideration on the grounds that she hadn't earned it. "I'm a rockstar now," she told the audience, before closing the night with "Jolene" alongside Brandi Carlile, Annie Lennox and Judas Priest's Rob Halford.

items.title: Barry Keoghan to Lead and Produce ‘Top Boy’ Prequel Series ‘Jonny Boy’ at Netflix (Exclusive)
items.summary:
Netflix has greenlit "Jonny Boy," a five-episode prequel set in the world of the British crime drama "Top Boy," with Barry Keoghan starring and executive producing. Keoghan will reprise the role of Jonny McGee, the Irish drug partner to Kane Robinson's Sully, who was introduced in the show's final season.

Cowboy Films is producing, and "Top Boy" creator and writer Ronan Bennett is returning to write. Ali Abbasi, whose credits include "The Apprentice" and "The Last of Us," will direct, with filming scheduled to begin in 2027. Aubrey Graham — Drake — who executive produced the original series, is back in that role, joined by executive producers including Charles Steel and Alasdair Flind for Cowboy Films, Adel Nur for DreamCrew, and Maverick Carter and Jamal Henderson for SpringHill Studios.

Keoghan and Des Byrne, who founded Wolfcub Productions together, said the series began with them. "We pitched our vision and idea to Netflix and the executive producers, and they were so supportive in wanting to bring our passion project forward, exploring Jonny McGee's origin story through a new bold lens," they said.

The Hollywood Reporter, which broke the news, reported that Netflix U.K. content vice president Anne Mensah announced the order during her spotlight session at the Edinburgh TV Festival on Wednesday afternoon.

"Top Boy" ran its first two seasons on Channel 4 from 2011 to 2013 before the broadcaster dropped it. Netflix revived the series in 2017 after Drake expressed interest, with Ashley Walters and Robinson returning as Dushane and Sully, and it ran three more seasons on the streamer. The fifth and final installment, which introduced Keoghan's character, aired in 2023, and the show won the BAFTA TV Award for best drama in 2024.
